posts.text:
Almost every country on Earth calls itself a democracy.

The red ones don't even bother.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ This map isn't measuring whether elections are free. It's measuring a claim — whether a state describes itself as democratic in its constitution, its official name, or its own official language.

Almost all of them do.

2/ Start with the red. Saudi Arabia's Basic Law of 1992 states that the system of government is monarchy, and that the Quran and the Sunna are the constitution. No election is promised anywhere in the text, and none is claimed.

3/ The UAE is a federation of seven hereditary emirates. Oman is an absolute monarchy under a sultan. Neither pretends otherwise. Afghanistan went furthest — under the Taliban it renamed itself the Islamic Emirate, dropping "Republic" entirely.

4/ Now the blue, where it gets strange. North Korea's full name is the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Algeria is the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria. Laos is the Lao People's Democratic Republic. East Germany was the German Democratic Republic.

5/ Indexes that measure the actual machinery — competitive elections, independent courts, a free press — consistently find that well under half the world's population lives under a functioning democracy.

The gap between this map and that number is the whole story.

6/ It wasn't always the magic word. In the 18th and 19th centuries "democracy" was often used as an insult, a synonym for mob rule. Many of America's founders preferred "republic" and meant the distinction seriously.

7/ After 1945 the word flipped. Democracy became the only respectable source of legitimacy on Earth — so governments with no intention of holding a free election claimed it anyway.

A label everyone wants tells you little.
